To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the notion of interventional consistency of a representation is an important property that has not yet been considered in the literature, and that the training scheme that we propose can be used to improve the quality of the representations learned by AE, VAE and SAE.

1) current metrics for disentanglement do not capture the quality of the learned representation; 2) the quality of the disentanglement is not a property of the learned representation, but of the encoder-decoder pair; and, 3) the quality of disentanglements is not captured by the reconstruction error, but by the consistency of the representation with respect to the interventions.

(i) the current conceptual tools used to assess disentangled representations (e.g. disentanglement scores) are inadequate, (ii) we introduce the notion interventional consistency of representations and argue that it should be a desirable property of representations, (iii) we propose a training scheme for auto-encoders that takes interventional consistency into account in the optimality conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: \textbf{Q1.} What are the limitations of existing tools for measuring disentanglement of a representation? \textbf{ Q2. } What is the role of intervention in the disentanglement criterion?
the following: (1) We propose a novel training scheme for auto-encoders, that takes into account the notion of interventional consistency in its optimality conditions.
the following questions: (i) What are the desirable properties of a representation? (ii) Are current methods able to capture them?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, while all three autoencoders are able to produce representations which are consistent under interventions, the VAE is the most consistent one among the three, and the SAE is the most inconsistent one.
, in general, autoencoders do not produce disentangled and robust representations, and that the only way to achieve this is to explicitly incorporate these notions into the training objective.
interventional consistency is a desirable property for the representation and the proposed training scheme can be used to achieve it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel optimality condition for autoencoders and demonstrate its effectiveness on three different architectures.

the interventional consistency is a fundamental property of any representation that can be learned in an unsupervised manner, and that the proposed training scheme is a general approach to achieve this.
, in order to achieve disentangled representations, one needs to consider the notion of interventional consistency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current notion of disentangled representation is not well-defined, and that interventional consistency should play an important role in its definition.
the notion of interventional consistency of the representation should be considered as the primary objective in designing autoencoders for disentangled representation learning.
interventional consistency is an important property of the optimal representations and it should be accounted for when designing learning schemes.
